full_judgment: 3. The plaintiff's case put in a nutshell is that Surendra Nath was the owner of 2.19½ acres of land having his two annas share out of 17.56 acres described in schedule under Sriram Mouza in SA khatian No. 1151. He was owning and possessing the land as ejmali. After the death of Surendra, his wife Maynamoti and daughter Jharna inherited the property. Moynamati as widow became owner of her share till lifetime. On 25-5-1982 and 15-7-1987 Moynamati sold 0.84 acres and 0.82½ acres of land respectively to the plaintiff No. 1 for her legal necessity. On the same date Moynamati again sold 0.14½ acres of land to the plaintiff No. 2 and delivered possession thereof. Thereby the plaintiffs acquired 1.81 acres of land by registered kabala deeds. One Purnandu Brahman co-sharer of late Surendra Nath and Jharna Rani and her husband Balaram Halder were the witnesses. The plaintiffs are owning and possessing 1.74 acres of land and they mutated their names and opened new khatian being No. 115½. On 26-6-1996, the defendant No. 1 disclosed that they obtained two registered kabala deeds from defendant No. 4 Basu Dev Halder, who had no legal right to transfer the land. Hence the suit.
